commit.message:
PEP in measles is buggy regarding the timelines (#253)

## Problem

The measles PEP intervention was buggy regarding the timelines.
Eligibility for MMR/IG was decided by comparing *each recorded contact
day* against the *index case's infectious-onset date*:

```cpp
int infectious_since = date_infectious[t_i];            // rash onset - prodromal period
...
(contact_day > infectious_since) &&
((contact_day - infectious_since) <= pep_mmr_window)
```

That measures the interval between the index becoming infectious and the
day a given classmate met it — not the quantity that matters. The MMR/IG
window is a *"is there still time to intervene?"* window: it runs from
the **exposure** to **today**, the day the case is identified and PEP is
given. With a realistic `mmr_window = 3` the old code did not behave as
intended; it only looked right because the tests used windows of
100–300.

## What the intervention does now

**Dating the exposure.** Given an index case with rash onset on day `d`,
public health considers it infectious from `d - prodromal_period` (this
is `date_infectious`, already computed by `ModelMeaslesSchool`). The
reference date is the **first** day, on or after that, on which the
class actually encountered the index:

```
              first_seen
              v
 |------------|=====================|.............| today
 ^            (index in school and infectious)     (case identified)
 infectious_since
              |<------- days_since = today - first_seen ------->|
```

Contact tracing is used only to *date* that first encounter, never to
decide who was exposed. This matters when the class is not in session
every day: if the contact rate is zeroed out on weekends (via a global
event) and the infectious window opens on a Saturday, the following
Monday anchors the window, not Saturday.

**The exposed cohort.** Public health does not have time to trace
individual contacts; the exposed group is treated as exposed as a whole.
For the single-school model that means the entire school. PEP is offered
to every agent in a PEP-target state, not only to the index's recorded
contacts.

**Several cases at once.** The earliest first encounter wins — a
co-detected case whose rash started earlier dictates how much time is
left.

**No double dosing.** Agents already holding a PEP tool are skipped. IG
still wanes, after which they become eligible again.

## Bug found along the way

`QuarantineTrigger` only refreshes its triggering set inside
`add_triggering_agent`, so on days with no detection it still held the
previous one — and the PEP global event, which runs daily, kept
re-administering PEP for a detection that happened days earlier
(observed firing every single day with an unchanging `first_seen`). The
intervention now treats that set as a queue: it takes today's detections
and empties it.

This is deliberately fixed inside `include/measles` rather than in
epiworld core, because the measles R package vendors `include/measles`
but takes epiworld core from epiworldR — a core change would block the
downstream package until epiworldR ships a new epiworld. Verified that
the downstream patch compiles against the *current* epiworldR.

## Consequences worth reviewing

Whole-school PEP is substantially more aggressive than before. In `14g`
the average number of recipients goes from ~60 to ~898, and mean
outbreak size from 32.6 to 24.0.

At **100% willingness** the entire school is dosed and released on the
very day it is quarantined, so the quarantine compartments are never
occupied at a day boundary. `14f` therefore now runs at partial
willingness, and the effective-PEP transitions are asserted from the
*pre-quarantine* state (`Latent -> Recovered`, `Prodromal -> Recovered`,
neither of which can occur through the natural disease history) rather
than from the quarantine states. At realistic willingness (0.8)
quarantine still binds normally.

PEP uptake is properly gated by the window now (avg recipients,
`days_undetected = 3`):

| window (mmr=ig) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 6 | 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| recipients | 317 | 622 | 780 | 844 | 898 | 898 |

## Tests

`tests/14i-measles-pep-timeline.cpp` drives `operator()` with hand-built
exposure histories and covers the five rules deterministically:
first-encounter within window doses the whole school (including agents
never recorded as meeting the index); an old first encounter denies PEP
even when the class met the index again yesterday; encounters before
infectious onset are ignored; the earliest of several co-detected cases
governs; and the weekend case. It fails on the previous logic.
`14f`/`14g` pass, and the suite builds in the school, mixing and
risk-quarantine contexts and under `EPI_DEBUG`.

Downstream sync: UofUEpiBio/measles#48.

## Optionally restricting PEP to the case's group

Offering PEP to the entire population is right for a single classroom,
but misleading for a population that is really a set of separate
communities: a case in one classroom does not expose the school next
door.

`InterventionMeaslesPEP` now takes an optional trailing group-membership
vector, one entry per agent, indexed by agent id:

```cpp
measles::InterventionMeaslesPEP<> pep(..., target_states, eff, ineff, agent_groups);
```

- **Empty (the default) = current behaviour.** The whole population is
treated as a single exposed group. `14f`/`14g`/`14i` are untouched and
reproduce their previous numbers exactly.
- **When given,** PEP is offered only to agents sharing a group label
with an identified case.
- **Each group is dated from its own exposure.** Previously the earliest
first-encounter across all co-detected cases governed everyone; now a
stale case in one classroom no longer denies PEP to a classroom exposed
yesterday. This falls out of the same code path — ungrouped simply means
one bucket, so `_group_of()` returns 0 for everybody.
- Labels are arbitrary integers (only equality matters). A vector whose
length is neither 0 nor `Model::size()` throws `std::length_error`,
since it is indexed by agent id.

This is model-agnostic: the risk-based quarantine model can pass class
affiliation directly, and the school model can impose classrooms on an
otherwise unstructured population.

New `tests/14j-measles-pep-groups.cpp` covers the default, restriction
to the case's group (either group), independent per-group timing, both
groups dosed when both are recent, arbitrary labels, and the length
check. Neutralising the grouping makes it fail. Downstream:
UofUEpiBio/measles#48.

Add ContactTracing::get_contacts() for per-agent contact iteration with lazy caching (#255)

`ContactTracing` only exposed a low-level indexed API
(`get_contact(agent, idx)`), making it cumbersome to iterate all
contacts for an agent grouped by who they contacted and when. This adds
a higher-level `get_contacts()` API matching the pattern described in
the issue.

## New API

**`ContactRecord`** — new class returned by `get_contacts()`:
- `get_contact_id()` → `size_t` — id of the contacted agent  
- `get_times()` → `const std::set<int>&` — all simulation days the pair
made contact

**`ContactTracing::get_contacts(size_t agent)`** → `const
std::vector<ContactRecord>&`
Groups the circular buffer contents by `contact_id`, collecting all
recorded days per unique contact into a `std::set<int>`. Result is
cached per-agent and invalidated automatically on the next
`add_contact()` call for that agent.

```cpp
auto & ct = model.get_contact_tracing();
for (auto & agent : model.get_agents())
{
    for (const auto & contact : ct.get_contacts(agent.get_id()))
    {
        size_t contact_id = contact.get_contact_id();
        const std::set<int> & when = contact.get_times(); // e.g. {0, 5, 20}
    }
}
```

## Implementation

- **`contacttracing-bones.hpp`**: Added `ContactRecord` class; added
private `cached_contacts` (`vector<vector<ContactRecord>>`) and
`up_to_date` (`vector<bool>`) members; declared `get_contacts()`.
- **`contacttracing-meat.hpp`**: Constructors and `reset()` initialize
cache members; `add_contact()` sets `up_to_date[agent_a] = false`;
`get_contacts()` lazily rebuilds via `std::map<size_t, std::set<int>>`
grouping.
- **`tests/30b-contact-tracing.cpp`**: Tests correct grouping, multi-day
aggregation, empty agents, cache identity (same address on repeated
calls), cache invalidation, and cross-verification against the existing
`get_contact()` API.
